why: handleQueue/handleBatch in src/server/queue.ts and src/server/batch.ts only dispatch to the exact same domain/factory handler functions used for direct tool calls (which each run their own evaluatePolicies/checkWritePolicy checks) and resolve $N.field via a plain regex string substitution, so this meta-tool introduces no sink or policy bypass of its own.

The caller-controlled email flows into credentialPath()/emailToSlug() in src/executor/paths.ts, which strips every '/' and '\\' character before use, so no '../' segment can survive to escape the fixed credentials directory, and authenticate/scopes require server-side GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET env vars rather than caller input.

Reviewed the factory generator (src/factory/generator.ts), calendar.yaml manifest, and src/services/calendar/patch.ts's customHandlers (agenda/freebusy/create/delete/update) — every operation composes a params object forwarded through the fixed-host Google API client (src/google/client.ts), with no filesystem, subprocess, or eval sink anywhere in the service.

Reviewed contacts.yaml and src/services/contacts/patch.ts (buildPerson, beforeExecute hooks) plus the batch body builders in src/server/batch.ts; all paths end at Google's People API through the shared client seam with no local file/command sink, and the tool's own account cannot be granted more than Google's OAuth scopes already allow.

Reviewed docs.yaml and src/services/docs/patch.ts's customHandlers (get/write/insertText/replaceText) — all build Google Docs batchUpdate request bodies and call the shared API client; no filesystem, subprocess, or eval sink exists in this service.

upload's customHandler (src/services/drive/patch.ts:124-127) lets an absolute filePath skip resolveWorkspacePath's sanitizer via isAbsolute(), but the very next line calls verifyPathSafety(filePath), which independently requires fs.realpath(filePath) to lie inside the workspace directory for any file that exists; any real absolute path outside the workspace throws 'Symlink escape detected' before readFile ever runs, so the bypass is inert for exfiltrating files outside the sandbox (confirmed by tracing src/executor/workspace.ts's verifyPathSafety, which has no exemption for the isAbsolute case).

Every header value (to/cc/bcc/subject) passes through sanitizeHeader() in src/services/gmail/mime.ts, which strips all CR/LF/control bytes before RFC 5322 assembly, and workspace-facing file ops (attachments, archive) go through resolveWorkspacePath+verifyPathSafety with no isAbsolute-style carve-out.

Reviewed meet.yaml and src/services/meet/patch.ts (beforeExecute prefixConferenceParent/Name, customHandlers) — a read-mostly browsing service whose operations only build Google Meet API request params through the shared client seam; no local sink found.

sink: setByPath (called from ScratchpadManager.jsonSet/jsonInsert in src/server/scratchpad/manager.ts on the JSON.parse()'d scratchpad buffer) writes params.value to a property resolved by walking the caller-supplied path segments with no denylist for '__proto__', 'constructor' or 'prototype'.
why: operation:'json_set' (or json_insert/json_delete) with path:'$.__proto__.<key>' on a format:'json' scratchpad reaches setByPath in src/server/scratchpad/json-path.ts. Because the intermediate object has no OWN '__proto__' data property (a fresh {} buffer), the bracket-access `current[String(segments[i])]` in the traversal loop (line 47) returns the object's real inherited [[Prototype]] (Object.prototype itself) rather than a plain data field, and the final assignment on line 54 then writes the caller's value directly onto Object.prototype. I extracted the exact parsePath/setByPath logic (verbatim from json-path.ts) into an isolated Node script (not the target repo) and confirmed Object.prototype.polluted becomes 'gotcha' process-wide after one json_set call, invisible in the tool's own JSON.stringify output since it's not an own property. Neither json-path.ts nor manager.ts contains any '__proto__'/'constructor'/'prototype' filtering (verified by grep). Impact is global to the running MCP server process (integrity of every plain object thereafter, including safety/config checks that read possibly-undefined properties), not merely a crash. The precise CWE is CWE-1321 (Prototype Pollution), which is not in the given taxonomy; CWE-915 (Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes) is the closest listed analog.

Reviewed sheets.yaml and src/services/sheets/patch.ts's customHandlers (updateValues body-shaping, create) — every operation builds a Google Sheets API request through the shared client; writing arbitrary cell values/formulas is the tool's advertised purpose and the sheet itself is the caller's own resource, so there is no local sink.

src/services/tasks/patch.ts only has a beforeExecute guard on 'update' that refuses an empty patch body; every operation is a direct, fully-typed field forwarded to the Google Tasks API with no filesystem/command/eval sink.

sink: fs.writeFile / fs.mkdir / fs.rename in src/server/handlers/workspace.ts (write, mkdir, move, compress, decompress) follow the OS path including any symlinked parent directory once verifyPathSafety has been skipped.
guard: partial: verifyPathSafety(filePath) resolves fs.realpath(filePath) and rejects anything outside the workspace, but only when the target path already exists; if the final component does not exist yet, fs.realpath throws ENOENT and the function returns success unchecked (workspace.ts:190-193), so a write/mkdir/compress/decompress to 'existingSymlinkedDir/newfile' never has its parent-directory symlink validated.
why: Traced resolveWorkspacePath -> verifyPathSafety -> fs.mkdir(dirname, {recursive:true}) -> fs.writeFile in the 'write' case of src/server/handlers/workspace.ts: if a directory inside the workspace were already a symlink to an external path, writing a NEW file under it would skip the realpath check (ENOENT on the not-yet-existing full path) and fs.writeFile would then follow the symlink outside the sandbox. I could not find any operation exposed by manage_workspace, or by any other tool in this shard, that creates a symlink inside the workspace (move/mkdir/compress/decompress only rename or write regular files/directories), so I cannot confirm the precondition (a pre-existing symlink placed there by something other than this tool) is reachable purely through caller-controlled arguments — hence Tier B rather than A.
contract: list: show files (recursive) | read: get file content | write: save content to file | delete: remove file or directory | move: move or rename a file/directory | mkdir: create a directory | compress: gzip a file | decompress: gunzip a file
